answer: A mechanism that actually bites: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because orchard only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, anchor is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any basalt approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
